newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures retreat, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures retreat, seen consolidating.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures retreated to end broadly lower on Monday in moderate dealings centred on AAs.
Traders said the market could consolidate around current levels after last week's spectacular jump on heavy fund short covering.
"It's marking time a little time, consolidating perhaps," said one. "After all the activity, it is trying to digest it a little bit."
Most-active March stood $31 lower at $1,289 a tonne by the close after bouncing off from what some traders said a key support at $1,280.
"The fund covering has been filled over the last week," the trader said.

"After seeing a fairly dramatic rise over a couple of days last week the market needs time to consolidate and settle," he added. "As long it can hold in here without too much drama, then it's looking reasonable."
Turnover reached 3,598 lots, mainly dominated by AAs on the March contract.
Technically, further major chart support is seen at $1,750 and an upside objective is pegged at $1,335 basis March.
The March contract's steep $80-gain last Wednesday on fund-induced rally helped inject some optimism in previously weakening technical charts.
But traders said that a further rally could be hampered by producer selling from Vietnam, Indonesia and Africa.

There was no fresh fundamental news but traders said the market focus would centre on a trade meeting in Vietnam this week and the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) meeting in Brazil next week.
Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze, leading a high-level African delegation to Vietnam gathering, is due to speak on Wednesday.

African producers said they would discuss robusta output with key non-ACPC producer Vietnam ahead of the ACPC meeting on January 23. Gauze is also expected to urge Vietnam to join the ACPC's export programme but traders doubt if Hanoi would sign up.
